about.title: Fort Jones Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Fort Jones is a small Siskiyou County community, but workplace injuries still happen here — on ranches, in shops along Main Street, at job sites near Rt 3 and SR-3, or on properties like those along Highway 3. Most of the time, California's workers' compensation system is the exclusive path for an on-the-job injury, meaning fault usually doesn't matter and lawsuits against your employer are generally off the table. But when a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to your injury, a separate third-party claim may be possible alongside your workers' comp benefits. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we're a free service that connects injured workers in and around Fort Jones with an independent attorney who can look at both angles of your situation, explain your options in plain terms, and help you understand deadlines before they pass.

items.title: We Understand the Exclusive Remedy Rule
items.desc: California generally requires injured workers to go through workers' comp rather than sue their employer directly, but that doesn't rule out every legal avenue. The attorney we connect you with can review whether a third party — like a contractor or equipment maker — also bears responsibility.

items.title: Deadlines Matter, Especially Near Fort Jones
items.desc: You typically need to report a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days, and any separate third-party claim carries its own 2-year deadline. Acting promptly helps protect your options in either direction.

items.title: Retaliation Protections Are Real
items.desc: California law prohibits employer retaliation against workers who report injuries or file workers' comp claims. If you're worried about your job, an independent attorney can explain your rights before you decide anything.

items.question: I was hurt working near Highway 3 outside Fort Jones — can I sue my employer?
items.answer: In most cases, California workers' compensation is the exclusive remedy against your employer, regardless of who was at fault. However, if another party — such as a subcontractor, equipment supplier, or another driver — contributed to your injury, a separate third-party claim may be available. An independent attorney can review the details to see which paths apply to you.

items.question: How long do I have to report my workplace injury?
items.answer: California law generally requires you to notify your employer within 30 days of the injury. Missing this window can complicate your workers' comp claim, so it's best to report as soon as reasonably possible after the incident.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for filing a workers' comp claim in Fort Jones?
items.answer: No — retaliating against an employee for reporting a workplace injury or filing a workers' comp claim is illegal under California law. If you believe you've faced retaliation, an independent attorney connected through LawProactive can help you understand your options.
